Hmm, but which subset is the compiler happy with? The example claimed the full set for a durable run without child calls. With a child call, durability properties may be undischarged. Dropping deterministic/retry_safe/idempotent is reasonable.

Let me submit with the trimmed set.","tool_calls":[{"index":0,"id":"call_00_85js7G1gJzy4EFKWw3Me9325","type":"function","function":{"name":"propose_change_set","arguments":"{"changes": [{"file": "handler.ts", "content": "import { run, step } from \"zttp:durable\";\nimport { call } from \"zttp:workflow\";\n\nstructural OrderWorkflowProof<T> = Proof<T,\n  | \"state_isolated\"\n  | \"result_safe\"\n  | \"optional_safe\"\n  | \"no_secret_leakage\"\n  | \"no_credential_leakage\"\n  | \"input_validated\"\n  | \"pii_contained\"\n  | \"injection_safe\"\n  | \"canonical\"\n  | \"cost_bounded\"\n>;\n\nexport function handler(req: Request): OrderWorkflowProof<Response> {\n  const key = req.headers.get(\"idempotency-key\");\n  if (key === undefined) {\n    return Response.json({ error: \"missing idempotency-key\" }, { status: 400 });\n  }\n  return run(key, () => {\n    const reservation = step(\"reserve_inventory\", () => {\n      return { reserved: true };\n    });\n    const notified = call(\"notify\", {});\n    return Response.json({ notified: notified.status }, { status: 201 });\n  });\n}\n"}]}"}}]},"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"tool_calls"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":13271,"completion_tokens":1036,"total_tokens":14307,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":4096},"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":618},"prompt_cache_hit_tokens":4096,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":9175},"system_fingerprint":"a26a7955944dc5c60445bff77fac9c8e"}
